The problem

Small teams drown in small tasks.

In a business of two to twenty people, nobody has a spare pair of hands. The owner ends up doing data entry at 9 p.m., invoices go out late, and good inquiries sit unanswered in an inbox until the customer calls someone else. None of that work needs a human. It just needs a system.

Where the week actually goes

Typical repetitive work we find in Mason County businesses on a first visit:

  • Copying orders, bookings, or forms into another system by handDAILY
  • Answering the same customer questions by email and phoneDAILY
  • Chasing unpaid invoices and late pickupsWEEKLY
  • Re-typing the same information into quotes and proposalsWEEKLY
  • Hunting for a number across email, paper, and three appsCONSTANT
  • Building the same report, list, or roster from scratchMONTHLY

What it costs you

It is rarely one big expense. It is death by a thousand small ones:

  • Slow replies that quietly lose sales and bookingsREVENUE
  • Late invoices that stretch your cash flow thinCASH FLOW
  • Typos and copy-paste errors that take hours to unwindREWORK
  • Evenings and weekends spent on paperwork, not familyTIME
  • Good employees quitting over mind-numbing busyworkPEOPLE
  • Knowledge trapped in one person's head and inboxRISK
💡

The fix is not more software. Most businesses already own tools that can do this work. The fix is connecting them, teaching an AI assistant your answers and your voice, and putting a human approval step where it matters. That is exactly what we build.

Services

What we build for you.

Six kinds of work, usually starting with one small, high-value project and growing from there. Everything is documented in plain English, and everything is yours — your accounts, your data, your systems.

01

AI assistants that answer like you do

A trained assistant for your website, inbox, or phone that answers customer questions using your real information — hours, prices, policies, directions, availability — and hands off to a human the moment it should.

  • Website chat trained on your business, not the whole internet
  • Email drafts written in your voice for your approval
  • After-hours answers so inquiries never sit overnight
  • Clear handoff rules: what the AI may say, and what it never touches
02

Workflow automation

The connective tissue between the tools you already pay for. When one thing happens — an order, a booking, a signed form — the next five things happen on their own.

  • Orders, bookings, and forms flow straight into your books and lists
  • Automatic confirmations, reminders, and follow-ups by email or text
  • Invoice reminders that go out on schedule, every time
  • Review requests sent at the right moment after a job well done
03

IT consulting & support

Straight answers on the technology decisions small businesses actually face, from someone local who will still be here after the sale.

  • Computers, networks, Wi-Fi, printers, and point-of-sale sorted out
  • Backups that actually get tested, and passwords done right
  • Honest advice on what to buy, what to skip, and what to cancel
  • Security basics: updates, two-factor sign-in, scam-proofing your inbox
04

Websites & online presence

A website that works as hard as you do — accurate, fast, easy to update, and wired into your booking, ordering, and mailing list instead of sitting there like a brochure.

  • New sites and clean-ups of existing ones, including Shopify stores
  • Online booking, ordering, and waitlist or allocation sign-ups
  • Google, map, and directory listings checked and corrected
  • Email lists and newsletters that send without a wrestling match
05

Documents, data & bookkeeping help

Turn piles of paper, PDFs, and spreadsheets into information you can search, sort, and trust — and keep the books fed without the Sunday-night data entry session.

  • Receipts and invoices captured, categorized, and filed automatically
  • QuickBooks and spreadsheet clean-up, with systems that stay clean
  • Customer, inventory, and job lists merged into one reliable source
  • One-click reports: sales, inventory, who's overdue, what's selling
06

Training & hand-holding

Technology only pays off if your people actually use it. We train your team in person, in plain English, and leave behind simple written guides for the way your business does it.

  • On-site training sessions for owners and staff
  • Plain-English cheat sheets for every system we build
  • AI skills for everyday work: drafting, summarizing, researching
  • A local number to call when something does not look right

    In practice

    Three automations, start to finish.

    No black boxes. Every automation we build follows the same honest pattern: something triggers it, the system does the legwork, a human approves anything important, and you can see a record of all of it.

    The invoice that chases itself

    For anyone who bills after the work is done.

    1. Job finished — you mark it done, once.
    2. Invoice created automatically from the job details.
    3. Friendly reminders go out at 7, 14, and 30 days, in your tone.
    4. You are only looped in if a customer replies or a bill goes past due.

    SAVES: THE AWKWARD FOLLOW-UP CALLS

    The inquiry that never sits overnight

    For shops, lodging, tasting rooms, and services.

    1. A question arrives on your site, email, or social page — at 2 p.m. or 2 a.m.
    2. Your AI assistant answers from your real hours, prices, and policies.
    3. Booking or order links are offered while interest is hot.
    4. The full conversation lands in your inbox for morning review.

    SAVES: THE SALES THAT WENT TO VOICEMAIL

    The week that schedules itself

    For appointments, tastings, crews, and deliveries.

    1. A booking comes in and lands on the right calendar automatically.
    2. Confirmations and reminders go out by text and email.
    3. No-shows drop because rescheduling is one tap, not a phone call.
    4. Your day view is ready each morning: who, where, and what to bring.

    How it works

    Start small. Prove it. Then grow it.

    No six-month contracts, no rip-and-replace. We start with the one task that annoys you most, prove it works, and build from there.

    Step 1 · Visit

    Discovery visit

    We come to you, watch how the work actually flows, and ask a lot of questions. You talk, we take notes. About an hour, at your place of business.

    Step 2 · Map

    Automation map

    You get a plain-English list of what could be automated, what each item would save, and what it would cost — ranked by payoff, so you choose where to start.

    Step 3 · Build

    Build & test

    We build your first automation, test it alongside your real work, and tune it until it sounds like you and behaves like you would want.

    Step 4 · Support

    Train & support

    Your team gets trained in person with written cheat sheets. Then we check in, watch the numbers, and add the next automation when you are ready.

    How we work

    Local, plain-spoken, and on your side.

    🤝

    A person, not a portal

    When something breaks or confuses you, you call a local person who knows your business and has stood at your counter — not a ticket queue in another time zone.

    Your accounts, your data, your customer lists, your logins. We build inside your tools wherever possible, so nothing is held hostage if we ever part ways.

    AI is fast and occasionally confident and wrong. Anything that spends money, makes a promise, or speaks for you publicly gets a human set of eyes first.

    If we cannot explain what a system does in one clear paragraph, it is too complicated to run your business on. Jargon is a cost, and we do not bill you for it.

    Your business data stays yours

    We set up AI tools so your customer information and trade details are not handed around carelessly, and we will tell you plainly what each tool does with data.

    We recommend what fits, including “keep what you have” when that is the right answer. Our living comes from work that keeps paying off for you, not from commissions.

    Mason is home base, and most clients are a short drive in any direction. On-site visits matter here: half of what we fix, we find by watching the work happen — the sticky note on the register, the second spreadsheet nobody mentioned, the password on the monitor.

    Questions

    Asked at almost every first visit.

    I'm not a “tech person.” Is this going to go over my head?+

    No, and that is by design. Most of our clients run great businesses and have no interest in becoming IT managers. We explain everything in plain English, train you in person, and leave written cheat sheets. If a system needs an engineer to operate day to day, it is the wrong system for a small business, and we will not build it.

    Do I have to replace the software I already use?+

    Usually not. Most projects start by connecting tools you already pay for — email, calendars, QuickBooks, Shopify, spreadsheets, your phone system. When something genuinely needs replacing, we will show you why, what it costs, and what you can cancel to pay for it.

    Will an AI say something wrong to my customers?+

    That risk is real with a careless setup, which is why we do not do careless setups. Your assistant answers only from information you approve, stays inside topics you set, and hands off to a human whenever a question falls outside them. For email and anything public, a person reviews before it sends until you tell us otherwise.

    What happens to my business and customer data?+

    It stays in your accounts, under your logins. We choose tool settings that keep your information out of public AI training wherever the tool allows it, and we will walk you through exactly what each tool does with data before we connect it. If a tool's data practices do not sit right with you, we pick a different one.

    How long does a first project take?+

    A focused first automation — an assistant, an invoice workflow, a booking flow — is typically a matter of weeks, not months, once we start building. Your automation map will give you a realistic timeline for your specific project before you commit to anything.

    Do you actually come out here?+

    Yes. Discovery visits, training, and anything hands-on happen at your place of business. Day-to-day support can be handled by phone or remote session when that is faster, but local means local: we are based in Mason and our clients are our neighbors.

    What does it cost?+

    It depends on the project, and anyone who quotes you a number before seeing how your business runs is guessing with your money. The automation map comes first: it produces fixed-price quotes for each build, ranked by what they save, so you can start with the one that pays for itself fastest.
